title: Towards Cross-lingual Values Assessment: A Consensus-Pluralism Perspective

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating discrepancies in LLMs' value-appropriateness assessments of Question-Answer pairs across diverse cultural contexts, judging whether models respect cultural pluralism versus imposing a single value stance.
Comparing the accuracy and consistency of LLM value assessments across 18 different languages against ground-truth labels provided by native speakers.
Testing LLMs' ability to neutrally and appropriately assess values in Question-Answer pairs within the 'Governance & Politics' and 'Sovereignty & Security' domains.
Evaluating model judgments on Question-Answer pairs categorized under 'History & Identity', assessing responses to national identity, historical disputes, and traditions.
Measuring the accuracy of LLMs in assessing the value-appropriateness of content related to the 'Ethnicity & Equity' domain.
Measuring the accuracy of LLMs in assessing the value-appropriateness of content related to the 'Belief & Expression' domain, which includes religious beliefs and pluralism.
Measuring the accuracy of LLMs in assessing the value-appropriateness of content related to the 'Gender & Rights' domain, including reproductive rights and LGBTQ+ issues.
